subject: math

objective.text: Use square tiles to compose a rectangle, and relate to the array model.

explanations.title: One row is an array
explanations.text: One row of tiles is also an array. 1 row of 10 is the same as 10 columns of 1. It is long and skinny.

explanations.title: Break a row in half
explanations.text: Break a row of tiles in half. Slide one half under the other. 10 tiles make 2 rows of 5. 14 tiles make 2 rows of 7.

explanations.title: Rows and columns give two equations
explanations.text: 2 rows of 5 gives 5 plus 5 equals 10. The 5 columns of 2 give 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 equals 10.

explanations.title: One number, many rectangles
explanations.text: The same number of tiles can make different rectangles. 12 tiles make 2 rows of 6 or 3 rows of 4. The total stays 12.

explanations.title: A square looks the same turned
explanations.text: A square array looks the same when you turn it. 4 rows of 4 does. 2 rows of 8 does not.

source_ref.section: Concept Development Part 2 (S: you can turn an array with 4 rows of 4)

examples.title: 10 tiles
examples.text: 1 row of 10. Or 2 rows of 5: 5 plus 5 equals 10. Or 5 columns of 2: 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 equals 10.

examples.title: 14 tiles
examples.text: 2 rows of 7. 7 plus 7 equals 14. Also 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 plus 2 equals 14.

examples.title: 16 tiles
examples.text: 2 rows of 8. Or break in half again to make 4 rows of 4. 4 rows of 4 is a square.

examples.title: 12 tiles
examples.text: 2 rows of 6, 3 rows of 4, or 4 rows of 3. All of them make 12.
